title: Derivative of profile times quantile
statement: Let $U(\alpha)=\varphi(Q(\alpha))$ be the Gaussian isoperimetric profile, where $Q$ is the lower standard Gaussian quantile and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density. For every $a\in(0,1)$, the function $p\mapsto U(p)Q(p)$ is differentiable at $a$ with derivative $1-Q(a)^2$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. For $a\in(0,1)$, the derivative of $p\mapsto I(p)Q(p)$ at $a$ is $1-Q(a)^2$.
